rows.explanation: Site on the steep flank of a peak. At surface level, terrain a few DEM cells upslope sets the Earth-facing horizon, so the result depends on sub-pixel position and on how an 80 m vs. 120 m grid resolves that slope. Our 0 m value sits at the bottom of PGDA's own range within ±2 px and our 2 m value is closer to PGDA, so 0 m fits worst here. Likely pixel-scale variability; no horizon error identified. Earth: PGDA within ±2 px 0.0–57.6 %; ours at 2 m: 15.6 %, 10 m: 38.8 %.

Massif summit site. The Sun result changes strongly between 0 m and 2 m, which points to near-field terrain setting the horizon. PGDA's own value varies widely within ±2 px. Likely pixel-scale variability; no horizon error identified. Sun: PGDA within ±2 px 10.9–55.6 %; ours at 2 m: 34.1 %, 10 m: 56.4 %.

method.sunDefinition: any part of the solar disc above the terrain horizon (Sun elevation + 0.265 deg)
method.earthDefinition: any part of Earth's disc above the terrain horizon (Earth elevation + its actual angular radius, about 0.95 deg)
method.pgdaDefinition: any part of the disc visible (product 69 labels)
method.sampling: hourly, 163048 h (18.6 years) from 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z; Sun/Earth vectors from the pinned SPICE kernels
method.claimLabel: agreement with PGDA under the any-disc definition, surface level assumed
method.notes: Observer height is an assumption: PGDA product 69 does not document its height, and surface level (0 m) is taken from Mazarico et al. (2011) for the 2010 maps, not confirmed for the 2016 rasters. The 2 m and 10 m runs are sensitivity checks only. Not accuracy against truth, and not height-matched. App metrics use other definitions.
